title: The Aztec and Inca states: tribute, roads and empire without iron or wheels
examples: How did the Inca run an empire without writing?
How did the Spanish conquer the Aztecs and Incas?

explain.say: When Spanish soldiers first saw Tenochtitlan in 1519, one later wrote that it seemed like a dream, a city rising from a lake. It may have held around 200,000 people, larger than any city in Spain. Look at the board: the Aztec and Inca states side by side.

draw.verdict: Two great states, each built in a century.

explain.say: Start with the left side. The Mexica, whom we call Aztecs, founded Tenochtitlan around 1325 on an island in Lake Texcoco and farmed chinampas, gardens built up from the lake bed. From 1428 a Triple Alliance with two other cities conquered widely and collected tribute: cloth, cacao, feathers and food. Why rule through tribute instead of governors everywhere?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Two great states, each built in a century.

explain.say: Now the right side. From 1438, under Pachacuti, the Inca expanded from Cusco along the Andes. Look at the map: from Quito in Ecuador to Chile. People paid tax in labour, the mit'a, working fields, building or serving in the army. Machu Picchu was built as a royal estate. Why might labour be easier to collect than money here?

See the network. Without writing or wheeled carts, the Inca ran their state with roads of around 30,000 kilometres, chasqui relay runners, huge storehouses and khipu, knotted strings that recorded numbers and perhaps more. Which link in the network surprises you most?

explain.say: Both fell fast to Spanish invaders: Tenochtitlan in 1521, helped by tens of thousands of Indigenous allies and smallpox, and the Inca after Atahualpa's capture in 1532, during a civil war. Brilliant work. Exam tip: explain the conquests with allies, disease and divisions, not just guns and horses.

faq.a: Estimates suggest around 200,000 people, perhaps more, in 1519, making it one of the largest cities in the world then. It sat on an island in Lake Texcoco, linked to land by causeways.
The capital of the Inca Empire, in the Andes of today's Peru, the centre from which roads ran to the four parts of the empire, Tawantinsuyu.

faq.q: How did the Inca run an empire without writing?
faq.a: They used khipu, knotted cords that recorded numbers like tribute and census counts and perhaps narratives, kept by trained specialists, along with roads, relay runners, storehouses and a labour tax.

faq.q: How did the Spanish conquer the Aztecs and Incas?
faq.a: Small Spanish forces exploited local divisions and gained huge numbers of Indigenous allies, such as the Tlaxcalans in Mexico. Epidemics like smallpox killed many, including rulers, and in Peru the Spanish struck during an Inca civil war.
asks: Why did the Aztec Empire fall?

faq.q: What was the Inca road system?
faq.a: The Qhapaq Ñan, a network of roughly 30,000 kilometres or more along and across the Andes, with bridges, way stations and storehouses, used by armies, officials and chasqui messengers. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
asks: How long were the Inca roads?

facts: Tenochtitlan fell to Spanish and allied Indigenous forces on 13 August 1521.
The Aztec Triple Alliance was formed in 1428.
Atahualpa was captured by Francisco Pizarro's forces at Cajamarca in November 1532.

quiz.why: Inca specialists recorded numbers, and perhaps more, with knots on cords.

wrong.1: Aztec temples were pyramids such as the Templo Mayor.
wrong.2: Khipu is an Andean word, nothing to do with ships.

quiz.say: Which factor helped Cortés most against Tenochtitlan, according to historians?

options.show: Tens of thousands of Indigenous allies
options.say: Tens of thousands of Indigenous allies

quiz.why: Allies like the Tlaxcalans provided most of the fighting force, alongside smallpox.

wrong.1: Spanish soldiers numbered only in the hundreds to low thousands.
wrong.2: Roads were not the decisive factor in Mexico.
